Open Start and type your company name and your own rules in the yellow cells: the days for the RSVP deadline and the head count lock, the seats at a table, the spare portions and the price per guest.
Check Events: the date, venue, guests and the phones of the client, venue, caterer and shuttle firm. The deadline, the lock date and the head count fill in by themselves.
Enter every invited guest on Guest List with the reply, meal, food restriction, access need, extra seats and table. The days to answer and the seat count fill in.
Keep RSVP Summary and Guest Groups current: they turn replies into a confirmed and an expected head count for the client and the caterer.
Record each seating request on Seating Requests and build the tables on Seating Tables. Over capacity tables and requests that need a change are flagged.
Write every food restriction on Dietary Register and every access need on Access Needs, and tick them off when the kitchen or the venue confirms.
Log each batch of invitations on Invitation Batches and each print order on Print Orders, and the reminders on RSVP Reminders.
Fill Shuttle Manifest, Room Block, VIPs and Speakers and Place Cards for the events that need them.
Lock the count on Final Head Count: the count for the caterer and the venue, the seats booked, and later the guests who came.
On the day, record each guest on Check-in Log. Afterwards, record gifts and thank-you notes on Gifts and Thanks.

Use the 14 calculators before you decide: head count, seats, tables and chairs, meals, empty seats, dates, invitations, shuttle, rooms, allergies, table balance, cost per guest, no-shows and a what-if grid.
Read Guest and RSVP Dashboard and Charts every week: replies, head count, seats, meals, allergies, invitations, no-shows and the cost of empty seats.

what went wrong, how it was fixed, how long it took and how many minutes of the programme were lost

what went well, what to change, a score and the vendors to rebook, with a flag for follow-ups still open

Run-of-show items: what happens at what time
One row per item of the day with start, length, owner and vendor, kept in time order for each event; the end, the gap to the next item and the overlap flag fill in by themselves.
Events with days to go and run-of-show state
One row per event with date, venue, lead and the finish time; the days to go, the run-of-show state, overdue milestones, the curfew check and the next event fill in by themselves.
Planning milestones with due dates and overdue flags
The key tasks of each event with owner, due date and the day done; the days to the due date, the days late and whether a milestone is on track, due soon, overdue or done late fill in.
Run-of-show templates for each kind of event
Ten steps for each of four templates, with the offset in minutes from the start of the main part, the length and who does it; the offset with buffers fills in and feeds the run-of-show builder.
Vendor arrival windows for each event
One row per vendor and event with the planned arrival and the load-in window the venue gives; the window length and whether the arrival is inside the window fill in.
Venue load-in, curfew and load-out deadline
One row per venue with the hour the load-in opens, the curfew, the load-out deadline and the noise limit; the minutes between the curfew and the load-out deadline and the open hours fill in.
Day-of team roster with hours and overtime
One row per team member and event with the role, the call time and the finish time; the hours worked after the break and the overtime over your shift limit fill in.
Contact sheet for the day with backup contacts
One row per role and event with the name, the phone and a backup contact; a flag shows every contact that has no phone number yet.
Packing and equipment list for each event
One row per item to pack with the quantity, the owner and whether it is packed and loaded; the ready state and the next event fill in so you see what is missing before the van leaves.
Weather risks, backup plans and decision times
One row per weather risk of an event with the trigger, the backup plan and the time you must decide by; the hours and minutes left to switch and the decision check fill in.
Emergency kit and emergency contacts with check dates
The items and on-call contacts you always carry, with where they are and the date they were last checked; the days since the check and an overdue flag fill in.
Floor plan zones with set-up minutes and times
One row per zone of the room in set-up order with what goes there and the minutes it takes; the start and finish time of each zone are counted from the hour the load-in opens.
Sound and lighting cues with times and operators
One row per cue with the time, the length, the operator and notes; the end time of each cue fills in so the sound and lighting person works from one sheet.
Programme slots and speeches against their time
One row per slot with the minutes allowed, the minutes really spoken and the microphone; the finish time and the over-time flag fill in so no speech eats the dinner.
Catering service schedule with staff per 50 guests
One row per course or station with the start, the guests, the minutes and the servers; the finish time, the staff per 50 guests and the dietary check fill in.
Transport timetable with trip minutes and seats
One row per run with where it goes, the departure and arrival times, the passengers and the seats; the trip minutes and whether the seats are enough fill in.
Issues on the day with the fix and the minutes lost
One row per problem on the day with what fixed it, who fixed it, how long the fix took and the minutes lost; a flag shows whether it was fixed within your limit.
Vendor check-in with minutes late and set-up on time
One row per vendor on the day with the planned and the real arrival and when the set-up was done; the minutes late, the late flag and the set-up check fill in.
Photographer shot list with the done check
One row per moment the photographer must capture with the group, the priority and the planned time; a flag shows shots that were done, missed or are still planned.
Post-event debriefs with the score and open follow-ups
One row per finished event with what went well, what to change, a score from 1 to 5 and the vendors to rebook; a flag shows follow-ups that are still open.
